fixes.explanation: The Jordan it is, friend! The LORD says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.” Moses, Israel's leader, has died, and the LORD tells Joshua, “Now therefore arise, you and all these people…” Big news. I'd need a minute to stretch before a message like that.

Ooh, I see why that sounds right, friend, but hold on. Look at the two little words in the middle: “just as.” The LORD tells Joshua, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. That promise was already made, so it's no brand new batch. It's an old recipe getting served.

Moses, Israel's leader, is the name the LORD gives. He says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” The first verse calls Joshua Moses' assistant, so Joshua had served alongside him. And then the LORD adds, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

Tents for the winter, friend? Now THAT is planning ahead! But winter never shows up in this message. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross the Jordan…” The people are told to get provisions ready, because the crossing is three days away. I'd have packed the tents too, and I'd have forgotten the provisions.

Ha, I know that one looked like a trick, friend! But that statement is right there in the text. Joshua tells those tribes, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So True was the answer, and the little word “may” is doing the heavy lifting.

Close, but that's not the job for the mighty men of valor. Joshua says the wives, young children and livestock “may remain” in the land Moses gave them. The mighty men are told something different: they “must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” That's the instruction Joshua gives them.
